name: Alaska
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+, with licensed stores operating since 2016.
summary: Alaska voters legalized medical cannabis in 1998 and adult-use cannabis in 2014 through Ballot Measure 2, which took effect in February 2015; the first licensed store opened in October 2016. Adults 21+ may carry up to one ounce and grow up to six plants. The state taxes cannabis at the wholesale level by weight ($50 per ounce of bud), and a 2026 bill to cut that tax (HB 91) stalled. In 2026 lawmakers approved sealing of old low-level possession convictions.

adult_use_since.value: Approved by voters Nov. 4, 2014 (Ballot Measure 2, 53% yes); possession became legal Feb. 24, 2015.

possession_limit.value: Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 ounce.

home_grow.value: Up to 6 plants per adult (no more than 3 flowering), with a cap of 12 plants per household with multiple adults.

public_use.value: Consuming in public is banned and can bring a fine of up to $100. Alaska was the first state to license on-site consumption at stores with a special endorsement.

retail_sales.value: Licensed retail sales began Oct. 29, 2016, when Herbal Outfitters opened in Valdez.

taxes.value: Excise tax is charged on growers by weight when product is sold to retailers or manufacturers: $50/oz for mature bud, $25/oz for immature bud, $15/oz for trim.

medical_program.value: Medical use is legal, but there is no separate medical retail channel or tax break; patients buy from the same licensed stores and pay the same tax.

regulator.value: Marijuana Control Board, staffed by the Alcohol & Marijuana Control Office (AMCO) within the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development.

hemp_thc.value: Since 2023, intoxicating hemp-derived products may be sold only through state-licensed marijuana stores; a federal judge upheld the restriction in May 2025.

timeline.event: Alaska Supreme Court holds the state privacy right covers small-amount possession at home
Voters approve Ballot Measure 2 legalizing adult-use cannabis
Adult possession and home grow become legal
First licensed store, Herbal Outfitters in Valdez, opens
Federal judge upholds Alaska's limits on intoxicating hemp products
Legislature passes omnibus crime bill allowing sealing of old low-level possession records; it became law without the governor's signature

pending.item: HB 91 would cut the per-ounce excise tax and replace it with a 6% retail sales tax.
pending.status: Stalled in the 2026 session; sponsor Rep. Ashley Carrick plans to reintroduce it next session.

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can legally possess up to one ounce and buy from licensed stores, which have operated since 2016.

faq.q: How many plants can you grow in Alaska?
faq.a: Adults may grow up to six plants, no more than three of them flowering, with a household cap of 12 plants when several adults live there.

faq.q: Can you smoke weed in public in Alaska?
faq.a: No. Public consumption is banned and can bring a fine. Some licensed stores hold an on-site consumption endorsement where use is allowed.

faq.q: How is cannabis taxed in Alaska?
faq.a: Alaska taxes cannabis by weight when growers sell it, at $50 per ounce of mature bud. A 2026 proposal to switch to a retail sales tax stalled.

faq.q: Do you need a medical card in Alaska?
faq.a: Not to buy cannabis, since adult-use is legal. Medical use is legal too, but there is no separate medical store channel or tax discount.
